title: A Receptor That Is Also an Address

scenes.tts: Can the protein that detects a smell also tell its axon where to go?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Receptor That Is Also an Address. Nose epithelium on the left, olfactory bulb on the right.
scenes.narration: Can the protein that detects a smell also tell its axon where to go?

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-one, Linda Buck and Richard Axel found the odorant receptor genes.
scenes.caption: In 1991, Linda Buck and Richard Axel found the odorant receptor genes.
scenes.visual: Credit: Buck and Axel, 1991. A receptor with seven helices crossing the membrane. On screen: 1991, more than a hundred genes in rat; later, about 1,000 in mouse.
scenes.narration: In 1991, Linda Buck and Richard Axel found the odorant receptor genes.

scenes.tts: In the nose, the rule is one neuron, one receptor, with rare exceptions.
scenes.visual: Rule 1 card: one neuron, one receptor. Each epithelial neuron tinted one colour.
scenes.narration: In the nose, the rule is one neuron, one receptor, with rare exceptions.

scenes.tts: Neurons with the same receptor are scattered within a zone of the nose.
scenes.visual: Blue-tinted neurons scattered among many others within one zone.
scenes.narration: Neurons with the same receptor are scattered within a zone of the nose.

scenes.tts: Yet their axons gather in a few glomeruli in the olfactory bulb.
scenes.visual: Blue axons cross into the bulb and converge.
scenes.narration: Yet their axons gather in a few glomeruli in the olfactory bulb.

scenes.tts: A glomerulus is a ball of neuropil, where sensory axons meet bulb neurons.
scenes.visual: Close-up of a glomerulus. Label: neuropil, a tangle of axons, dendrites and synapses with no cell bodies.
scenes.narration: A glomerulus is a ball of neuropil, where sensory axons meet bulb neurons.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, Peter Mombaerts and colleagues marked axons from neurons using the P two promoter.
scenes.caption: In 1996, Peter Mombaerts and colleagues marked axons from neurons using the P2 promoter.
scenes.visual: The P2 locus as a box with a blue marker. Credit: Mombaerts and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: In 1996, Peter Mombaerts and colleagues marked axons from neurons using the P2 promoter.

scenes.tts: They converged on two glomeruli in each bulb, one medial, one lateral. One receptor, about two glomeruli.
scenes.visual: Bulb outline: one blue glomerulus on the medial side, one on the lateral side. Rule 2 card: one receptor, about two glomeruli per bulb.
scenes.narration: They converged on two glomeruli in each bulb, one medial, one lateral. One receptor, about two glomeruli.

scenes.tts: The receptor protein also reaches the axon terminals. Could it be part of the address?
scenes.visual: Receptor icons on the axon terminal as well as the dendrite. Question mark.
scenes.narration: The receptor protein also reaches the axon terminals. Could it be part of the address?

scenes.tts: Predict. Delete the P two receptor, but keep the marker. Where do the axons go?
scenes.caption: Predict. Delete the P2 receptor, but keep the marker. Where do the axons go?
scenes.visual: On screen: Predict. P2 coding sequence removed; marker kept.
scenes.narration: Predict. Delete the P2 receptor, but keep the marker. Where do the axons go?

scenes.tts: They wandered, and failed to form a P two glomerulus. So the receptor is needed.
scenes.caption: They wandered, and failed to form a P2 glomerulus. So the receptor is needed.
scenes.visual: Blue axons wander across the bulb without converging. Credit: Wang, Axel and colleagues, 1998.
scenes.narration: They wandered, and failed to form a P2 glomerulus. So the receptor is needed.

scenes.tts: A caveat: neurons without a working receptor often switch on a second receptor gene.
scenes.visual: Caution card: receptor-less neurons often switch on a second receptor gene.
scenes.narration: A caveat: neurons without a working receptor often switch on a second receptor gene.

scenes.tts: Predict. Put the M twelve receptor in place of P two. Where do the axons go now?
scenes.caption: Predict. Put the M12 receptor in place of P2. Where do the axons go now?
scenes.visual: On screen: Predict. M12 coding sequence swapped into the P2 locus. The M12 glomerulus marked far away.
scenes.narration: Predict. Put the M12 receptor in place of P2. Where do the axons go now?

scenes.tts: They converged near the P two glomerulus, and far from M twelve's own.
scenes.caption: They converged near the P2 glomerulus, and far from M12's own.
scenes.visual: A new blue glomerulus forms near P2, not at M12.
scenes.narration: They converged near the P2 glomerulus, and far from M12's own.

scenes.tts: So the receptor helps choose, and other features of the neuron count too.
scenes.visual: Card: the receptor is part of the label, not all of it.
scenes.narration: So the receptor helps choose, and other features of the neuron count too.

scenes.tts: Here the shared label is the receptor itself. Unlike Sidekick, it is not known to bind matching receptors on other axons.
scenes.visual: Two blue axons side by side; no bond drawn between their receptors. Beside them, two Sidekick processes zipped together for contrast.
scenes.narration: Here the shared label is the receptor itself. Unlike Sidekick, it is not known to bind matching receptors on other axons.

scenes.tts: In layers and in self-avoidance, a match says same, and the cell decides what same means. Smell shares the logic of a shared label, but no receptor-to-receptor match is known; how the receptor sorts axons is still being worked out.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card returns: direct matching drawn only on the layer and self-avoidance panels; the glomerulus panel labelled analogy, receptor-dependent sorting.
scenes.narration: In layers and in self-avoidance, a match says same, and the cell decides what same means. Smell shares the logic of a shared label, but no receptor-to-receptor match is known; how the receptor sorts axons is still being worked out.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: in smell, receptor identity helps axons of one channel converge. Other features of the neuron count too.
scenes.visual: Closing card, olfactory axons only: receptor identity helps one channel converge; other features count too. Footer: activity refines these maps later.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: in smell, receptor identity helps axons of one channel converge. Other features of the neuron count too.
